# `silk/build/tasks`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The standard tasks a project's tasks.silk starts from: build, run, dev and plan.

`silk init` writes a tasks.silk whose `Build`, `Run`, `Dev` and `Plan` variants each call one
function here with the project's own compilation, so a setting the project makes once reaches
every command and the editor. Each variant embeds [`Options`](./build-options.md#Options), which gives it `--release`,
`--optimization none|speed|size`, `--target <triple>` and `--debug true|false`. `silk test`
stays the toolchain's own command.

## Examples
```silk
import silk.build.graph { Compilation, Options, BuildError }
import silk.build.tasks { Standard, StandardError }
import silk.cli.command { Command, CommandLine, Opt }
import silk.cli.task { Task, TaskSet }
import silk.collections.list { List }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator }
import silk.system.child_process { ChildProcess }
import silk.system.filesystem { FileSystem }
import silk.system.host_input { HostInput }
import silk.text.string { String }

union Tasks {
  Build { pub options: Options, pub out: String },
  Run { pub options: Options, pub arguments: List<String> },
  Dev { pub options: Options, pub arguments: List<String> },
  Plan { pub options: Options },
}

impl CommandLine for Tasks {
  static fn command() -> Command<Tasks> {
    return Command<Tasks>.make("tasks", "Build and run the program")
      |> Command.variant("Build", "Build the program (use --release to optimize)")
      |> Command.variant("Run", "Build the program and run it")
      |> Command.variant("Dev", "Run the program, and restart it when a source changes")
      |> Command.variant("Plan", "Write the editor compilation requests")
      |> Command.flatten("options")
      |> Command.option("out", Opt.about("Also copy the program to this directory"))
      |> Command.arg("arguments", Opt.about("Arguments for the program, after --"))
  }
}

effect fn compilation(options: &Options) -> Compilation
  ! BuildError
  ? &mut Allocator | &mut FileSystem | &mut HostInput {
  return run Compilation.fromPackage(options)
}

impl TaskSet for Tasks {
  effect fn perform(self: Tasks) -> ()
    ! StandardError
    ? &mut HostInput | &mut Allocator | &mut ChildProcess | &mut FileSystem {
    match move self {
      Tasks.Build { options, out } => run Standard.build(run compilation(&options), out.view())
      Tasks.Run { options, arguments } => run Standard.start(run compilation(&options), &arguments)
      Tasks.Dev { options, arguments } => run Standard.dev(&options, &arguments)
      Tasks.Plan { options } => run Standard.plan(run compilation(&options))
    }
  }
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ? &mut HostInput {
  return run Task.main<Tasks>()
}
```

Import as `Standard` with `import silk.build.tasks { Standard }`.

<a id="StandardError"></a>

## `StandardError`

```silk
pub type StandardError = BuildError
  | TaskError
  | ProcessError
  | FileError
  | HostInputError
  | OutOfMemoryError
  | WriterError
```

Every failure a standard task can end with, for the `perform` of a tasks program whose variants
call [`Standard`](#Standard): a failed build, a program that ended with a nonzero status, or a file,
process, environment, memory or output failure.

<a id="Standard"></a>

## `Standard`

```silk
pub struct Standard
```

The standard tasks. Each takes the project's compilation, made from the command's [`Options`](./build-options.md#Options),
so that one function of the project configures every task.

<a id="Standard.impl"></a>

## Implementation `Standard`

```silk
impl Standard
```

<a id="Standard.impl.build"></a>

### Associated function `build`

```silk
pub effect fn build(compilation: Compilation, out: string) -> ()
    ! BuildError
    ? &mut Allocator | &mut FileSystem | &mut HostInput
```

Builds `compilation`. Its artifacts stay at `build/<target>/<mode>/<name>`. When `out` is not
empty, they are also copied to the directory `out`, relative to the package directory, keeping
their names and permissions.

#### Errors
[`BuildError`](./build-graph.md#BuildError) when the compilation or one of its steps fails.

<a id="Standard.impl.start"></a>

### Associated function `start`

```silk
pub effect fn start(compilation: Compilation, arguments: &List<String>) -> ()
    ! BuildError | TaskError
    ? &mut Allocator | &mut FileSystem | &mut HostInput
```

Builds `compilation` and runs its program with `arguments`, sharing the task's terminal and
environment, and waits for it.

#### Errors
[`BuildError`](./build-graph.md#BuildError) when the build fails; [`TaskError`](./cli-task.md#TaskError) with the program's status when it ends
with a nonzero one.

<a id="Standard.impl.plan"></a>

### Associated function `plan`

```silk
pub effect fn plan(compilation: Compilation) -> ()
    ! BuildError
    ? &mut Allocator | &mut FileSystem | &mut HostInput
```

Writes the editor's compilation requests for `compilation` to `build/requests/`, without
compiling it.

#### Errors
[`BuildError`](./build-graph.md#BuildError) when a step the requests need fails.

<a id="Standard.impl.dev"></a>

### Associated function `dev`

```silk
pub effect fn dev(options: &Options, arguments: &List<String>) -> ()
    ! TaskError | FileError | HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator | &mut FileSystem | &mut HostInput
```

Runs the project as `silk run` does, with `options` and `arguments`, and restarts it each time
a file under the package's `src/` or its `silk.toml` changes. A build that fails is reported
and the next change tries again. It ends when the task is stopped, such as with Control-C,
and stops the program first. It needs macOS or Linux.

#### Errors
[`TaskError`](./cli-task.md#TaskError) when `SILK_COMPILER` or `SILK_PROJECT_ROOT` is not set, as outside `silk`, on
another system, or when the program cannot be started.
